tasks.title: Understand responsible AI principles
knowledge: Recognize risks and limitations of generative AI in software development
Understand ethical usage of AI coding assistants
Identify potential harms from AI-generated code (security, bias, copyright)
Describe mitigation strategies for AI-generated code risks
Understand responsible AI frameworks applicable to developer tools
skills: Evaluate AI-generated code for ethical and safety implications
Apply responsible AI principles when using Copilot
Identify when AI suggestions may introduce risks or biases
Make informed decisions about when to accept or reject Copilot suggestions

tasks.title: Validate and operate AI tools
knowledge: Understand the necessity of validating AI-generated output before use
Recognize that Copilot can produce hallucinations and incorrect suggestions
Know the principles for operating Copilot in a responsible and safe manner
Understand developer accountability for accepted AI-generated code
skills: Review and test AI-generated code before committing
Apply critical evaluation to Copilot suggestions
Operate Copilot as an assistant, maintaining developer oversight and accountability
Establish validation workflows for AI-assisted development

tasks.title: Use GitHub Copilot in the IDE
knowledge: Know how to enable GitHub Copilot in VS Code (Status Bar > Use AI Features and sign in), JetBrains IDEs, Visual Studio and other supported editors
Understand the ways to trigger Copilot: inline suggestions, Copilot Chat (Ask, Plan and Agent), inline chat, Copilot CLI and agent mode
Know how to use agent mode for multi-step tasks that edit files and run tools with approval
Understand how content exclusions behave in the IDE (supported for inline and chat; not supported in VS Code Edit and Agent modes)
skills: Enable and sign in to Copilot in supported IDEs
Use inline completions, ghost text, next-suggestion navigation and inline chat
Interact with Copilot Chat using natural language, # context and slash commands
Invoke agent mode for complex multi-file tasks and review its changes
Recognize when a file is excluded from Copilot in the IDE

tasks.title: Use GitHub Copilot CLI
knowledge: Define GitHub Copilot CLI (the `copilot` command): an agent in the terminal that answers questions, writes and debugs code and works with GitHub.com

Know the install options: `npm install -g @github/copilot` (Node.js 22+), `winget install GitHub.Copilot`, `brew install --cask copilot-cli` or the install script; the old gh-copilot extension (`gh copilot suggest/explain`) was retired on October 25, 2025
Understand key features and commands: interactive vs programmatic mode (`copilot -p`), plan mode (Shift+Tab), slash commands such as `/model`, `/context`, `/compact`, `/mcp` and `/feedback`
Know tool approval and trust: per-tool approval, `--allow-tool`, `--allow-all-tools` and `--deny-tool` (deny wins), trusted directories
Know that organization policy can disable Copilot CLI for seat holders
skills: Install and sign in to GitHub Copilot CLI
Use Copilot CLI interactively and across sessions, steering it with plan mode and approvals
Run Copilot CLI programmatically in scripts with pre-approved tools
Generate scripts and manage files with Copilot CLI

tasks.title: Use GitHub Copilot features and capabilities
knowledge: Understand agent mode, Copilot Edits (multi-file edits, now made in agent mode in VS Code) and MCP servers for tools and data
Know how to manage agent sessions and delegate tasks to subagents, which run in their own context and return a focused result
Know Copilot cloud agent (formerly coding agent) and Copilot code review on pull requests
Understand Copilot Spaces (which replaced knowledge bases), GitHub Spark (retired on github.com in August 2026) and pull request summaries
Know customizable review standards and behavior via instructions files: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, AGENTS.md, personal and organization instructions
Understand Copilot Chat limits, options, feedback and commands, including reusable prompt files (`.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`)
skills: Use agent mode with MCP servers for multi-step development tasks
Delegate scoped work to subagents to keep the main context focused
Request Copilot code reviews and generate PR summaries
Set up instructions files and prompt files for consistent team-wide behavior
Use Copilot Spaces to ground answers in curated project context

tasks.title: Manage organization-wide settings and policies
knowledge: Know how organization owners manage Copilot policies (Settings > Code, planning, and automation > Copilot > Policies) and which surfaces each policy covers (IDEs, Copilot CLI, github.com)
Understand Copilot code review policies and feature availability across IDEs and github.com, including 'Copilot in GitHub.com' and 'Opt in to preview features'
Understand Copilot audit log events (`action:copilot`, `actor:Copilot`), 180-day retention and that prompts are not logged
Know the REST API for seats (`/orgs/{org}/copilot/billing`, `.../billing/seats`, `.../selected_users`, `.../selected_teams`) and that removed seats stay active until the end of the billing cycle
Know the Copilot usage metrics report endpoints (`/copilot/metrics/reports/...`, `day` in YYYY-MM-DD) that replaced the legacy metrics API on April 2, 2026
skills: Configure organization-level Copilot policies and model availability
Enable and configure Copilot code review policies for pull requests
Assign and remove Copilot seats using the REST API or GitHub UI
Monitor Copilot usage with audit logs and usage metrics reports

domains.title: Understand GitHub Copilot Data and Architecture

tasks.title: Describe data handling and flow
knowledge: Understand how user code (prompts) flows from IDE to GitHub Copilot servers
Know how context is collected and assembled into the prompt sent to the LLM
Understand the role of the Copilot proxy in filtering and processing
Know data sharing policies: what data is transmitted, retained, and used
Understand how suggestions are post-processed before being returned to the IDE
skills: Explain the end-to-end data flow from IDE input to suggestion display
Describe how prompts are constructed from editor context
Identify where data is filtered and processed in the Copilot pipeline
Apply knowledge of data handling to make informed privacy decisions

tasks.title: Understand lifecycle and limitations
knowledge: Understand the complete code suggestion lifecycle from trigger to display
Know fundamental LLM limitations: context window, hallucinations, training data cutoff
Understand the probabilistic nature of LLM outputs
Know why Copilot may produce outdated, incorrect, or insecure suggestions
skills: Describe the full lifecycle of a Copilot code suggestion
Apply knowledge of LLM limitations to evaluate suggestion quality
Identify when Copilot suggestions are likely to be outdated or incorrect
Use validation strategies to compensate for LLM limitations

domains.title: Apply Prompt Engineering and Context Crafting

tasks.title: Craft effective prompts
knowledge: Understand prompt structure and the elements of an effective Copilot prompt
Know how Copilot determines context from the active file, open tabs, and workspace
Understand zero-shot prompting: task without examples
Understand few-shot prompting: task with 2–5 concrete examples
Know prompt engineering best practices: specificity, descriptive naming, type annotations
skills: Write specific, context-rich prompts that produce accurate suggestions
Use descriptive variable and function names as natural prompt engineering
Apply few-shot examples to teach Copilot non-standard patterns
Structure comments to maximize Copilot suggestion quality

tasks.title: Engineer prompts for performance
knowledge: Understand prompt engineering principles: specificity, single responsibility, context richness
Know the Copilot prompt process flow: user input → context → model → response
Understand how chat history is used across a conversation session
Know when to attach a specific file with `#`, search the workspace with `#codebase`, or use other context such as `#selection` (the `@workspace` participant is deprecated in VS Code)
skills: Apply single-responsibility prompting for complex multi-step tasks
Use prompt process flow knowledge to engineer higher-quality prompts
Leverage chat history strategically within a Copilot Chat session
Reference specific files, selections and workspace context with `#` references and `#codebase`

Understand how Copilot assists with refactoring and code modernization

Understand how Copilot accelerates developer learning in unfamiliar codebases

Apply Copilot Edits for refactoring and code modernization tasks
Generate docstrings, README sections, and inline documentation with Copilot
Use Copilot as an in-IDE learning tool for unfamiliar frameworks and APIs
Generate realistic test fixtures and mock data using Copilot

tasks.title: Support testing and security
knowledge: Understand how Copilot generates unit tests and integration tests
Know how Copilot identifies edge cases and boundary conditions
Understand how to generate test assertions with Copilot
Know how Copilot suggests security improvements in existing code
Understand performance optimization use cases with Copilot
skills: Generate unit and integration tests for existing functions using Copilot
Use Copilot to identify and test edge cases and boundary conditions
Write comprehensive test assertions with Copilot assistance
Use Copilot to identify and suggest security improvements
Apply Copilot for performance optimization in algorithms and queries

domains.title: Configure Privacy, Content Exclusions, and Safeguards

tasks.title: Manage privacy settings and exclusions
knowledge: Know how to configure content exclusions at the repository, organization and enterprise levels (Copilot Business and Enterprise)
Understand content exclusion path syntax (fnmatch, case-insensitive; repository references or `"*"` at org level)
Understand output ownership: GitHub does not own inputs or outputs (Generative AI Services Terms)

Know the limits of outputs: possible public-code matches, defence of IP claims depending on your agreement, and that blocking public-code matches is no longer required for Microsoft's Customer Copyright Commitment (April 3, 2026)
Understand individual settings (such as 'Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training' on Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max) versus organization policies
skills: Configure repository-level and organization-level content exclusions
Write correct glob patterns to exclude sensitive files and directories
Apply content exclusions for credentials, proprietary algorithms, and PII-containing files
Validate that content exclusions are working correctly after configuration

tasks.title: Apply safeguards and troubleshoot
knowledge: Know how to enable 'Suggestions matching public code' (Allow or Block) for users, organizations and enterprises
Understand what public code matching does (about 150 characters compared with public GitHub code; block or show code references)
Know how to troubleshoot missing suggestions and connection errors (status, logs, network checks, proxy and certificate settings)
Understand how to troubleshoot content exclusions (up to 30 minutes to propagate, reload the IDE, check rules at every level, unsupported modes)
Know audit log events related to Copilot for governance oversight
skills: Enable and configure the public code filter in organization or enterprise settings
Troubleshoot missing suggestions by checking exclusion rules at every level
Resolve content exclusion issues (reload the IDE, verify paths, allow for propagation)
Monitor Copilot policy changes using GitHub audit logs
